title: Constructible sheaves over a discrete Noetherian ring form a weak Serre subcategory
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], meaning that it has a finite affine open cover by spectra of Noetherian rings, and let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], regarded as discrete. On the small étale or small pro-étale site of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], use sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf $\underline R$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Call a sheaf constructible if there is a finite stratification [def-constructible-stratification] of $X$ by constructible locally closed subschemes on each of which it is locally constant with finitely presented $R$-module values [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. On either site the constructible sheaves contain zero and are closed under kernels and cokernels of morphisms between constructible sheaves, and under extensions: if $0\to F\to E\to G\to0$ is exact and $F,G$ are constructible, then $E$ is constructible. In other words they form a weak Serre subcategory, with the displayed closure properties as its meaning. No finiteness of the underlying set of $R$ and no invertibility on $X$ is assumed.
